name: One-Sided Criterion for Empty Unique-Midpoint Core
statement: For nested ample families $A\subseteq B$, let $\kappa_A(B)$ be the largest $W\subseteq B\setminus A$ such that every $w\in W$ roots a unique-midpoint constraint in $B$ whose two heads lie in $A\cup W$. It is computed by pruning roots with no such witness while retaining $A$ and keeping the original constraint set fixed. Now split ample $H$ in an active coordinate into sections $B_0,B_1$ with overlap $A$. If both ordinary section cores are empty and $\kappa_A(B_i)$ is empty for either side, then the ordinary unique-midpoint core of $H$ is empty. In particular this holds if either section corner-peels to $A$, equivalently if either inclusion $A\subseteq B_i$ admits an $A$-relative ample chain.
proof: Unions of relative cores are relative cores, so the pruning procedure leaves their unique largest member. Assume $\kappa_A(B_0)$ is empty and let $K$ be a core of $H$. A root in the exclusive zero wing has no vertical neighbour, so its witness is horizontal; projection would put it in $\kappa_A(B_0)$, which is impossible. Any remaining zero-section root projects into $A$. A vertical witness for it would require a head in the excluded zero wing, so every witness is again horizontal; the zero section of $K$ would then be an ordinary core of $B_0$ and must be empty. The same argument makes the one section a core of $B_1$, hence empty. Finally, if $B$ corner-peels to $A$, the first deleted member of any nonempty relative core would still have both witness heads present and could not be a corner, a contradiction.
comments: One side suffices. The archived control has relative-core orders 52 and 0 over its two sections and empty global core, while an empty global core can also coexist with two nonempty relative cores.
